package.title: 8 Targets, Jump 2/3: What Do Random Dots Draw?
alt_titles: A Million Random Jumps Draw A Carpet Of Holes
The Sierpinski Carpet From Pure Chance
description: Put 8 targets on a square: the 4 corners and the 4 edge midpoints. Pick one at random and jump 2/3 of the way to it. Repeat a million times.
The dots draw the Sierpinski carpet: a square with a hole, eight smaller squares with holes, and so on forever. Fractal dimension log 8 / log 3 = 1.893.
Change the rule and it changes completely:
4 corners, jump halfway → the square just fills up evenly
Every dot here is a real jump.
package.question: Which rule surprised you most? 👇
package.pinned: The carpet has zero area but infinite perimeter of holes. Dimension 1.893: more than a line, less than a plane 🟦
